review:
Apply the following identity check as the final review of the preserved findings.
For each deferred callback, handle or stored reference, distinguish the captured
object or value from a later lookup through a mutable wrapper or key. Follow
identity from creation to invocation and attribute admission, success, cleanup
and generation checks to the object that actually receives each effect. Numeric
generation equality alone does not establish object identity. Where the boundary
permits it, compare unchanged identity with copying, object replacement, mutation
of a referenced wrapper/key, and rebinding of only the caller's local variable.
Keep these operations distinct. State starting objects, ordered operations and
observable outcomes; cite capture and use sites. Retain all earlier ordinary
success, failure, cancellation and repeated-call findings while adding identity
variants. Do not assume replacement is a defect when stable capture or an identity
guard prevents redirection. Cite documented exclusions; leave silent intent open.

Preserve ordinary success, failure, cancellation, and repeated-call controls. For each deferred action, handle, or stored reference, identify what is captured and what is looked up later. Keep separate creations distinct and trace each from creation through use and cleanup, citing capture and use sites and stating the starting objects, operation order, and observable outcomes. Where permitted, compare unchanged identity, copying, replacement, wrapper or key mutation, and caller-local rebinding as distinct operations. Attribute each check and effect to the object that receives it. Require evidence beyond equal generation values to establish identity, and account for stable capture and identity guards. Cite documented exclusions and leave policy questions the source does not answer marked OPEN.

Keep ordinary success, failure, cancellation, and repeated-call controls, including actions created after cancellation. Trace each distinct creation through use and cleanup. Cite where references are captured or resolved later, state the starting objects and event order, and attribute each check and effect to the object it reaches. Distinguish return values, their causes, and when deferred work starts or finishes. Where permitted, test unchanged identity, copying, replacement, wrapper or key mutation, and caller-local rebinding separately. Verify identity with evidence beyond matching generation values and account for stable captures and identity guards. Cite documented exclusions and mark unanswered policy questions OPEN.
